correctness.summary: The shifted two-point functional follows from the same cardinal representation as the source and still annihilates the one-dimensional sampling kernel for even periods. Retaining the exact maximum coefficient gives the stated admissibility certificate. Endpoint singularity subtraction plus digamma identities yields the weight asymptotic, and one-variable optimization gives the phase-dependent exponent and Euler-constant half-shift coefficient.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The direct 2026 source gives the half-shift cyclic functional and an explicit non-optimized lower bound, but does not state the optimized Euler-constant coefficient, the asymptotically optimal period, or the shifted-phase family. Searches found no equivalent robust-interpolation refinement. Classical cosecant-sum asymptotics are treated as known ingredients rather than claimed novelty.

value.summary: The result exactly optimizes a natural explicit obstruction mechanism from the source, improves its published leading lower-bound coefficient by a factor about 32.1, and explains why the half-period shift is uniquely distinguished among fixed shifted two-point functionals by the optimal pi/2 exponential coefficient.

limitations: The asymptotic equivalent concerns the explicit shifted cyclic certificate, not the true epsilon_Ch parameter.
The order-H gap between the known upper and lower bounds for the true parameter remains open.
Only fixed phases are classified; no claim is made about all periodic functionals or H-dependent phases.
No quantitative threshold in the grid size is obtained.
The originality assessment is literature-based and contemporaneous unindexed work remains possible.
Independent audit has not been performed.
